text:
anna: FYI canary for hawthorn-9b-v2 (int4) is OOM-ing in the canary pool after warmup. Repro on two nodes.
leo: saw the alert, can you paste the stack/logs? rough counts (tokens) where it blows up?
anna: logs below — happens around token 820-930 on a few requests. Not a single huge prompt.
```
[2025-11-02T14:12:03Z] Exception: OutOfMemoryError: allocate 1.2GB failed
model=hawthorn-9b-v2-int4 node=canary-ml-07
kv_cache_usage: 0.84
fragmentation_est: 0.28
batch_size=4 latency=95ms
max_new_tokens=512
```
sam: thanks. quick hypothesis: quant int4 + batching = KV cache pressure + slab fragmentation.
maria: did quality change after int4 quant? we pushed quant artifacts earlier in the canary, right?
anna: small quality delta on long-form (BLEU-like QA tests): -0.9% mean across our eval set. Int8 looked fine.
leo: fragmentation_est 0.28 is suspicious but not catastrophic. where is prefetch/prefill set?
david: linking kernel/alloc notes — we saw similar pattern with cedar10b when max_new_tokens stayed high and continuous batching allowed >8 inflight. solution then was to reduce default max_new_tokens and enable kv-evict soft thresholds.
anna: current model config in canary: 
```yaml
model: hawthorn-9b-v2-int4
batching:
  max_batch_size: 8
  batch_window_ms: 20
prefetch: true
max_new_tokens: 512
kv_eviction: off
soft_eviction_threshold: 0.9
```
leo: can we try a minimal change set? 1) lower max_new_tokens -> 256 2) set batching.max_batch_size -> 4 3) enable kv_eviction with trim_percent=0.12 4) disable prefetch for canary nodes (to reduce transient mem spikes)
maria: agree. also flag for QA: run the quant vs int8 eval slices for the same prompts (long-turn convers.), we need to verify the -0.9% is consistent and not noise. If quality delta > 1.5% we fallback to int8 locally.
sam: i can run a quick throughput bench on canary with those settings. expecting some latency variance but hopefully no OOMs. will post numbers in ~30m.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: change-set hawthorn-int4-canary-20251102-01 by anna. Will apply to canary pool in 5m.
anna: running with patch now (small canary). if stable, we can roll to wider dedicated pool and run A/B (50/50 int4 vs int8) under load.
david: extra idea — enable slot_compactor background sweep (interval=60s) on these nodes to reduce slab fragmentation; cheap and safe for canary.
leo: +1 for slot_compactor, but watch latency p95. add tracing.
anna: quick bench results after patch:
```
config: max_new_tokens=256, max_batch_size=4, prefetch=false, kv_eviction=enabled
throughput: 2350 req/min (+3% vs int8 smallbatch)
latency p50: 92ms p95: 220ms
OOMs: 0 (ran 2k requests across 3 nodes)
quality: delta vs int8 = -0.4% (down from -0.9) on long-turn eval
```
maria: good improvement on OOM. quality delta acceptable for now but keep an eye. schedule 24h drift check and regen eval every 6h for the next day.
sam: will keep canary at 10% traffic with those settings and start automated quality monitoring hooks. if regressions hit >1% for 3hrs -> auto-fallback to int8 for the model.
david: follow-up: we should add a model-specific default profile for hawthorn-9b-v2-int4 to codify these safer defaults (max_new_tokens=256, batch_window_ms=12, kv_eviction=on, slot_compactor=1m).
anna: created PR for profile + tests: https://git.internal/redwood/ml-profiles/pull/412 (link in case you want to review)
leo: nice. one more telemetry ask — add per-token memory trend traces to canary dashboards so we can spot slow leak vs fragmentation.
maria: +1. also add a bench comparing cost/tok vs int8 for 24h to confirm e2e unit economics.
anna: summary: patched canary -> OOMs resolved, small quality hit reduced, follow-up actions: add profile PR, enable slot_compactor, update dashboards & auto-fallback. I'll open follow-ups for each. :thumbsup:
leo: thanks — will monitor p95 and fragmentation. ping me if it pops again.
anna: thanks team!
